name: Garganega

lines.s10: Garganega is the grape of Soave, from the hills east of Verona: lemon, white peach and a clean finish of bitter almond.
lines.s20: Garganega makes Soave, the dry white of the hills east of Verona. It tastes of lemon, white peach and ripe pear with a finish of bitter almond, and the hillside wines of Soave Classico add a stony depth.
lines.s45: Garganega is the grape in every glass of Soave, grown on hills of dark volcanic rock and pale limestone east of Verona. It tastes of lemon, white peach and ripe pear, and it finishes on a note of bitter almond. It is dry and light to medium in body, with a gentle freshness. Most of it is made in steel tanks and bottled young, with no oak to hide the fruit. Pour it with risotto, lake fish or white asparagus. Dried on racks through the winter, the same grape becomes Recioto di Soave, a golden sweet wine that tastes of honey.
lines.sale: Garganega, as a Soave from the hills, is the white for a creamy plate: lemon and white peach to lift it, bitter almond to close it. I would pour it with the risotto, or with the redfish and a squeeze of lemon.

glass.lead: Lemon, white peach and ripe pear with acacia blossom, soft and dry, closing on bitter almond and a stony edge.

ladder.where: The hills of Soave Classico and Gambellara
The Verona plain in a hot summer, and Sicily as Grecanico

glass.structure: Dry. Acidity medium, brighter from the hills, alcohol moderate, body light to medium; Recioto di Soave, from dried grapes, is sweet and full.

home.home: The hills and plain east of Verona, in the Veneto. Soave must be at least 70 per cent Garganega, with Trebbiano di Soave or Chardonnay for the rest, and Gambellara next door grows the same grape. The vines are trained high on pergolas and ripen late. Soave Classico, from hills of volcanic basalt and limestone, is the wine that keeps.
home.abroad: It scarcely leaves Italy. In Sicily the same vine is called Grecanico Dorato, as DNA work has shown, and it goes into the island's dry whites. Outside Italy it is a rarity.

service.temp: 45 to 50 degrees Fahrenheit, 7 to 10 degrees Celsius; a Soave Classico at the warmer end.
service.glass: A white wine glass; a small glass for the sweet Recioto di Soave.
service.decant: No. A light white with no oak needs only to be cold and freshly opened.
service.age: Most within two or three years; Soave Classico from the hills can keep ten.

with.dish: Risotto with peas or spring vegetables
with.why: a gentle wine beside a gentle, creamy dish

with.dish: Lake fish or trout, simply cooked
with.why: lemon and almond season the fish
soft acidity sits easily beside asparagus
a light white leaves the fish its sweetness

with.dish: Almond tart, with Recioto di Soave
with.why: the sweet wine echoes the almond

labels.means: A town and its wine zone east of Verona; the wine is at least 70 per cent Garganega.
From the historic hill zone around Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, on volcanic basalt and limestone.
A separate DOCG for hillside Soave made to stricter rules; not the same thing as Classico.
Sweet golden wine from Garganega dried on racks for months; the Veneto's first DOCG, in 1998.
Sicily's name for the same vine, in full Grecanico Dorato.

guest.q: Is Soave a grape or a place?
guest.a: A place: a town east of Verona and the hills around it. The grape is Garganega, which must make up at least 70 per cent of the wine.

guest.q: I remember Soave as thin and plain. Has it changed?
guest.a: That was mostly wine from the heavily cropped plain. Ask for Soave Classico from the hills, where old vines on volcanic rock and limestone give white peach, almond and a stony depth.

guest.q: What is that slightly bitter taste at the end?
guest.a: Bitter almond, the mark of the grape. It is meant to be there, and it is one reason Soave sits so well beside rice, fish and anything creamy.

compare.tell: Pinot Grigio from the same corner of Italy is lighter and more neutral, pear and lemon alone; Garganega adds white peach and a finish of bitter almond.
Verdicchio is sharper and leaner, with higher acidity, lemon and green almond; Garganega is softer and rounder, with white peach.
Cortese, as Gavi, is leaner and more lemony, with green apple and a stony finish; Garganega is softer, with white peach and more almond.

profile.st: Pale lemon, gold as Recioto · Body light to medium · Acid medium · Alcohol moderate · Dry, or sweet from dried grapes
profile.fruit: Lemon zest, white peach, ripe pear; yellow apple and apricot from limestone and from riper sites
profile.other: Bitter almond and marzipan, acacia blossom and elderflower; a chalky or smoky finish from the hills; honey in Recioto di Soave
profile.tell: A soft, dry Italian white of lemon and white peach that ends on bitter almond, with no oak: Soave, and from the hills a stony depth
profile.regions: Soave and Soave Classico, Gambellara and the Custoza blend in the Veneto; Sicily as Grecanico Dorato
profile.confuse: Pinot Grigio is lighter and more neutral; Verdicchio is sharper, with higher acidity; Cortese is leaner and more lemony; Garganega is rounder, with white peach and bitter almond

cards.front: Garganega: which wine does it make, and how much must the blend hold?
cards.back: Soave, from the hills and plain east of Verona. At least 70 per cent Garganega, with Trebbiano di Soave or Chardonnay allowed for the rest.

cards.front: What is Garganega called in Sicily, and how do we know?
cards.back: Grecanico Dorato. DNA work published in 2008 found the two names to belong to one vine.

cards.front: Garganega dried on racks through the winter makes which sweet wine?
cards.back: Recioto di Soave: golden and honeyed, from the same hills as dry Soave. It was the Veneto's first DOCG, in 1998.

questions.q: A blind white is pale lemon and dry, with lemon, white peach and ripe pear, no oak, gentle acidity and a finish of bitter almond. Which wine is it most likely to be?
questions.exp: Gentle acidity, white peach and a bitter almond finish with no oak point to Garganega from Soave. Gavi would be leaner and sharper, with green apple, and Pouilly-Fumé and Petit Chablis sharper still.

questions.q: A guest reading an Italian list asks what sets Soave Classico apart from a wine labelled only Soave. What do you tell her?
opts: It comes from the historic hill zone around the town
It is aged longer in oak before release
It is made from grapes dried on racks
It is made from Garganega with no other grape
questions.exp: Classico names the original hill zone around Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, on volcanic basalt and limestone. It is no rule of oak or of ageing, and dried grapes make Recioto di Soave.

questions.q: At the end of dinner a guest asks for a sweet wine from the same grape as the Soave she enjoyed. Which do you bring?
questions.exp: Recioto di Soave is Garganega dried on racks and made sweet. Recioto della Valpolicella is its red neighbour, from Corvina, and Moscato d'Asti and Vin Santo come from other grapes.

report: Mode home, as the plan fixes it: Soave and Gambellara in the Veneto, with Sicily (Grecanico Dorato) given as abroad, since a guest meets it under another name there and it is the same vine.

A thin grape: the profile is written in the manner of GRAPES. No Codex record is contradicted. The Codex already holds the 70 per cent minimum with Trebbiano di Soave and Chardonnay for the rest, the pergola and the late ripening, the basalt of Monteforte and the limestone of Soave, lemon, pear, almond and a chalky or smoky finish, Classico ageing a decade, Recioto di Soave as the Veneto's first DOCG in 1998, Gambellara, the Custoza blend, risotto, lake fish and white asparagus, and Grecanico as the same vine.

INTRO_GRAPES gives the aroma as white peach, almond, citrus blossom and marzipan. The entry keeps white peach, almond and marzipan and names the blossom as acacia and elderflower, which the consortium's white flower and several tasting notes support; citrus blossom is a family word the build refuses.
Orange zest, apricot and yellow apple: the consortium gives apricot, sweet apple and citrus for the limestone wines. Orange zest is a taster's reading of that citrus beside the lemon the Codex names.

The ladder is a taster's reading (the hills against the plain and Sicily). INTRO_GRAPES calls the grape's climate moderate, so the hills take the moderate rung and the hot plain and Sicily the warm one. No source read describes the taste of Grecanico in Sicily, so the entry says only that it goes into the island's dry whites.

Most Soave made in steel and bottled young: the common account; the consortium's rules were read through search results only, and a share of Soave Classico is raised in large casks, so the line says most and no more.

The DNA identity with Grecanico Dorato stands on the paper in Vitis of 2008 (two synonymous groups, Grecanico Dorato and Garganega) and on the Codex's own Régionale question. A study of 2003 is cited by secondary pages only and is left out.
Left out for want of a second source: the month of the harvest, the thickness of the skins, and how long the grapes for Recioto di Soave are dried.
The sources were read through search results; this session could not open the hosts directly (the consortium's site must be allowed in the network settings for a direct reading).
